title: Speech of President Arroyo during the Groundbreaking Ceremony of the Pantal Bridge
text:
Speech of Her Excellency Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo President of the Philippines During the Groundbreaking Ceremony of the Pantal Bridge

[Delivered at Brgy. Pantal, Dagupan City, Pangasinan, August 9, 2006]

Balbaleg ya salamat Speaker de Venecia. Thank you very much to the father of Pantal bridge and my super ally, Speaker Joe De Venecia.

Madame Gina de Venecia and my companions at mass earlier this morning, Congressman Tulagan and Espino; Ambassador Yamazaki and all our friends from Japan who have helped make this project a reality; our Cabinet members; our host mayor, Mayor Benjie Lim and the other officials of the City of Dagupan; Governor Agbayani and the other officials of Pangasinan and the other mayors who are here today to help us celebrate this beautiful affair; Commissioner Fernandez; all of the officials and people of Pantal and Dagupan, Masantos ya ngarem ed sikayon amin. Tuloy-tuloy so schedule ko ya bisita ed saray naduma-duman probinsya, tan malike-liketak imbita-an kayo a mila ed martsa, intayon amin paunla ed progreso na baley tayo.

Your Excellency, Ambassador to the Philippines Yamazaki, please relay to your government and people the deep appreciation for your continued support for Philippine development. Japan is by far the biggest source of official development assistance to the Philippines. And I thank you ambassador and the other Japanese guests for joining us in this groundbreaking and also for joining us later for lunch because I understand bangus is the favorite dish of Ambassador Yamazaki.

Ambassador Yamazaki told us about the almost 200 projects under this package, 200 projects amounting to eight billion pesos. But this one project alone is 800 million pesos, one-tenth of the whole package. So, this Pantal bridge, as said earlier by our different speakers, is the only long-span bridge of the bridges to be built nationwide under this Japan facility that’s why it cost much much more than the other smaller bridges. This is called Package III of the loans from Japan. Ayan tatawagen nga Package III met so sanka-unan ed samay apat era ya packages manlapo ed samay urgent bridges construction project for rural development, as Ambassador Yamazaki has explained to us, for the bridges of the rural areas of the Philippines. But Dagupan is not a rural area. It’s an exception to the rest of the bridges because Speaker de Venecia was so active in making sure that this bridge would be financed after 100 years of waiting by the people of Dagupan.

Para doon sa mga hindi namin kabaleyan na Pangasinan, itong Pantal bridge ay bahagi ng Dagupan bridge diversion road. Eto ay pet project ni speaker para maging mas maginhawa ang komersiyo dito. And this will increase the land area, the usable land area of Dagupan by one-third. Yes, and sa ganun itong bahagi ng bansa, gaya nang sabi ni Mayor Benjie Lim, hindi lang tutulong sa Dagupan kundi na rin sa buong Pilipinas. Dagdagan ang halaga ng Dagupan bilang sentro ng puhunan, trabaho, edukasyon lalo na sa hilaga o sa amyanan ng ating Luzon.

This is one of the big projects in our Medium-Term Public Investment Program.

Doon sa aking State of the Nation Address kwenento ko yung ilan sa mga programa sa MTPIP at sinabi ko na itong mga proyekto natin ihahati natin sa apat na sub-economy ng Pilipinas, panglima yung Cyber Corridor mula Baguio hanggang Davao. Why are we dividing the country into sub-economies? Because each super region has its natural advantages and we want to focus on these advantages so that we can speed up the programs vital to the main growth strategy and reduce the dependence on Imperial Manila.

Ang Dagupan, Bangus capital of the Philippines; of the world, reyna ng aquaculture sa North Luzon agri-business quadrangle. It provides not only bangus but other high-value fish not only to the rest of Luzon but also to the rest of North Asia including the country of Japan. Ang Dagupan at Pangasinan din ay mahalagang bahagi ng Cyber Corridor dahil napakarami ang inyong mga magagaling na kolehiyo. And I want to congratulate the people of Dagupan and Pangasinan for your excellent tradition of academic excellence.

Itong North Luzon agri-business quadrangle, ang kanyang pinakamalaking proyekto ay narito rin sa Pangasinan, yung Agno River Irrigation Project, ang halaga nito ay five billion pesos. At gusto ko rin ikuwento hindi lamang yon ang irrigation project sa Pangasinan meron ding ibat-ibang mga maliliit na irrigation project na humahalaga ng — there are 35 other irrigation projects — na humahalaga rin ng 354 million pesos. Papano natin napopondohan ito, papano natin napopondohan yung mga binanggit ko sa aking State of the Nation Address? Salamat, Joe, sa aking super ally, sa iyong liderato at suporta kaya mayroon tayong budget para dito sa mga malalaking proyekto na kailangan sa kaunlaran ng North Luzon agri-business quadrangle at buong Pilipinas.

Yung Medium-Term Public Investment natin over the rest of my term as president… Ah, hindi. Yung budget lang natin for year 2007 is more than one trillion pesos. And that is the economic dividend of the greatest fiscal reforms of our generation, achieved under the great leadership and support of the beloved son of Dagupan, Joe de Venecia and our other congressmen represented here today by Gener and Madz.

Nagbubunga na ang ating mahihirap na reporma sa ekonomiya at pananalapi ng bayan. And we not only successfully sourced funds for our programs, we also gained international confidence and support for current and future projects. And I am very very grateful to the government of Japan because they have more projects like this lined up for our Philippine future.

Noong isang linggo lamang nakatanggap tayo ng mahigit pitong bilyong dolyar na commitment ng Hapon, Tsina, World Bank at Asian Development Bank para pondohan yung ating mga super region kasama ang North Luzon agri-business quadrangle.

And while I thank the congressmen, I think I’d like to say also that I am happy that our senators heed well the voice of the people in suspending the investigation of the OWWA funds that after all had been certified by the COA as intact and readily available. Our OFWs stranded in Lebanon have to be served with our undivided attention until they are all rescued. Meanwhile, other national priorities have to be attended to.

Now for instance, we promote agri-business and commerce more aggressively through more and better infrastructure projects not only to the Pantal bridge, not only to Redios-Dagupan diversion but other major roads and bridges. At ito ang papel ng Pantal bridge. But aside from that, we also need other roads.

Every month we are allocating 500 million for farm-to-market roads all over the country — 200 million pesos are for the North Luzon agri-business quadrangle; 200 million para sa Mindanao; 50 million para sa mga ilang sasakahan ng Luzon Urban Beltway; at 50 million para sa Central Philippines.

Dito lang sa Pangasinan meron nang inapprove ng Regional Development Council ng labing anim na farm-to-market road amounting to 25 million pesos and counting. Sa buong Pilipinas naman, pinapalaki natin ang gastos ng mga serbisyong panlipunan gaya ng kalusugan, edukasyon, lalo na ang edukasyon sa Cyber Corridor kung saan ang Pangasinan ay isang malaking- malaking bahagi.

Our reforms are taking root and our growth is irreversible. Ang inyong pamahalaan ay nakatukoy sa kaunlaran.

Suporta-an tayon amin sirin so reporma ya mangiter na malakas tan progresibo ya Pilipinas.

Congratulations! Joe for this bridge. Thank you Ambassador Yamazaki.

Balbaleg ya salamat ed sikayon amin.
